info.name: Nasaq — Teachers, Students & Attendance
info.description:
Everything on the teacher and student side, end to end, plus both attendance modules.

**Run it top to bottom with NO ENVIRONMENT selected.** Every value is a collection variable; an environment variable of the same name would win and break the run.

Each run registers its own school with a timestamped slug, so nothing collides with a previous run or with real data. No copy-paste and no manual setup.

Set `baseUrl` once (collection → Variables) and press Run.

---

**Folders 09 and 10 are the ones that matter after a deploy.** They pin down behaviour that was broken and is easy to break again:

- **09.4** — a check-in with a forged `X-Forwarded-For` must be refused. If this passes, any teacher can check in from home and the record will claim they were on the school network.
- **10.1** — a student must not be able to mark anyone absent. If this passes, `AbilitiesGuard` has stopped being a global `APP_GUARD`.

Both failures are silent in normal use. Nothing errors; the wrong thing simply succeeds.

---

**Re-running individual requests**

Every run registers its own school, so a full run from 00.1 is always clean. Re-sending a single request against a school that already went through the folder can hit a legitimate rule instead — a class may only have one final exam per subject per year, a student may only sit an exam once, a teacher may only check in once a day. Those 400s and 409s are the system working, not a broken collection.

07.2 recovers from its own duplicate automatically. For everything else, **run from 00.1** when a step behaves oddly on its own.

item.name: 11 · Grade weights are school policy
item.description:
The weight distribution decides how 100 marks split across the final, quizzes, assignments, activities and projects, and it sets the subject's passing grade. Two students in 1/1 and 1/2 are compared against each other at promotion time, so they have to be measured with the same ruler — which means the distribution is set by the school, and a teacher works inside it.

Every request here used to pass. POST/PATCH/DELETE /gradesCriteria carried no @CheckAbilities, PATCH /schools/me/settings carried no role check, and POST /exams invented a criteria when none existed — handing the distribution to whichever teacher created the first exam.
